summary:
The report is that supervisord's optional TCP control interface
([inet_http_server]) lets an unauthenticated user read logs or restart
programs when it is enabled without a username and password. The
maintainer disputes this as a vulnerability: the interface is off by
default, enabling it without credentials is an explicit configuration
choice, supervisord logs a warning when it starts that way (supervisor/
http.py, "running without any HTTP authentication checking"), and the
documentation was updated to warn about it. No code change was made or
is planned, so no release fixes it.

Debian's /etc/supervisor/supervisord.conf in 4.2.5-3 defines only
[unix_http_server] on /var/run/supervisor.sock with chmod=0700 and no
[inet_http_server] section. Debian rates the CVE unimportant for the
same reason.
